Hard lines (non‑negotiable): Wave‑1 scope, the 90‑day exclusion for Customer Ops/Product, and the go/no‑go thresholds (attrition, engagement, realized savings); invite manager input on pacing, task sequencing, and local reassignment within those boundaries.  
Staged messaging: board gets the financial case and metrics, VPs get empowerment to localize within constraints and the expectation of weekly data submission, managers get empathetic, actionable scripts focused on role clarity, support resources, and immediate next steps.  
Top three people risks to monitor weekly: (1) regretted attrition in excluded/high‑risk functions — track weekly voluntary exits by name/role; (2) engagement erosion — track weekly pulse score and sentiment tags by function; (3) capacity/service degradation — track SLA breaches, escalation counts, and vacancy/coverage in critical roles.

I should stick to three main metrics for our dashboard: regretted attrition, engagement pulse, and realized run-rate savings vs. plan, including SLA impacts. For clarity, the weekly dashboard should show: 1) voluntary regretted attrition counts and names in high-risk functions, 2) weekly engagement scores by function, and 3) realized SG&A savings against the plan. A hard stop should trigger if regretted attrition exceeds three in 14 days or if there’s a 10-point drop in engagement. rounds.response:
Propose a one‑page weekly steering dashboard with three KPIs only: (1) regretted voluntary attrition (count + names) for Wave‑1 and excluded/high‑risk functions, (2) weekly pulse engagement by function, and (3) realized run‑rate SG&A savings vs plan plus one critical SLA for services we expect to protect.  
Hard‑pause triggers (single metric = pause): regretted attrition >3 people in any 14‑day window OR engagement drop ≥10 points in a function; a financial pause only occurs for a combined breach (run‑rate savings <20% of plan AND critical SLA degradation >30%); any lesser breach requires an immediate, time‑boxed remediation plan and deployment of pre‑approved mitigations.  
Board pre‑read language (concise): “Committed to a phased hub‑and‑spoke with 90‑day exclusions for frontline Customer Ops and Product, governed by a lean weekly dashboard and objective hard‑pause thresholds that protect people and service while preserving momentum; pre‑approved retention, workload relief and temp support will be deployed as needed.”

Proposed 12–18 month success scorecard (7 metrics): concise definitions and indicative targets (12‑month / 18‑month).  
1) SG&A run‑rate reduction (realized, annualized vs pre‑restructure baseline): target 4–6% at 12 months, 6–8% at 18 months.  
2) Operating margin (EBITDA margin, company‑wide): target +100–200 bps at 12 months, +150–350 bps at 18 months (directional, tied to SG&A captures and revenue stability).  
3) Regretted voluntary attrition (count of separations we judge mission‑critical, tracked rolling 30 days and annualized): target ≤ baseline at 12 months; improve ≥20% vs baseline by 18 months.  
4) Engagement pulse (function‑level weekly/quarterly score, net change vs baseline): limit drop to ≤2 points at 12 months and recover to +3 points above baseline by 18 months.  
5) Critical SLA adherence (composite of top 1–2 customer SLAs, % met): ≥95% at 12 months, ≥97% at 18 months.  
6) Customer experience (CSAT or NPS for core products; rolling 90‑day avg): maintain within −1 point at 12 months, +2–4 points improvement by 18 months.  
7) Service stability (backlog/throughput and error rate for core flows; TBD by Ops dashboard): backlog ≤ baseline +10% at 12 months and ≤ baseline −15% at 18 months; error rate down ≥10% by 18 months.  
Trade‑off language for the board and messaging: “Our north star is durable cost reduction plus preserved customer and people outcomes — we will accept up to a modest SG&A shortfall (~1–2 ppt) in a severe case if it prevents material regretted attrition or SLA failure; conversely, if SG&A targets are met but customer SLAs or regretted attrition deteriorate materially, we will reallocate savings and pause further cuts until remediation restores stability. Weekly steering will flag trade‑off states (e.g., ‘ahead on SG&A / behind on SLAs’) and recommend proportionate actions: tolerate small, temporary SG&A variance to protect people/service; require immediate remediation or rollback when service + people metrics cross hard thresholds. ”
